title: Set Matrix Zeros
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
pattern: use the matrix itself as marker storage
problemStatement: If an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0, in-place.
intuition: You cannot zero rows as you discover them — new zeros would cascade. So separate marking from writing, and store the markers in row 0 / column 0 to reach O(1) space.

approaches.title: Better: two marker arrays
approaches.idea: Record which rows and columns must be cleared, then apply.

approaches.title: Optimal: first row/column as markers
approaches.idea: One extra flag disambiguates column 0, whose marker cell is shared.
approaches.whyWorks: Writing bottom-up right-to-left consumes each marker only after it has been read.

edgeCases: Zeros already in row 0 or column 0
commonMistakes: Zeroing in the same pass as detecting, causing a cascade
Forgetting the separate flag for column 0
patternRecognition: O(1) space on a matrix -> store metadata in a border row/column
followUps: Use a single flag instead of two
What if 0 is a legal data value you must preserve elsewhere?
interviewInsight: The cascade bug is the point of this problem; name it before writing code.
